nodes.label: Runtime Mode Parity
nodes.description: Gameplay behavior is shared across Tauri, headless, and web runtimes through backend-agnostic orchestration; entry points are thin wiring.

nodes.label: Chat-First Illustrated Viewport

nodes.label: Mod-Driven Engine Content Separation
nodes.description: World, NPC, prompt, festival, encounter, transport, UI, and pronunciation content is loaded from mod packages so the Parish engine remains generic across runtimes.

nodes.label: Branching Journal Persistence
nodes.description: SQLite WAL storage combines append-only events, periodic snapshots, cross-process locking, and named branch histories to support crash recovery and alternate timelines.

nodes.label: Per-Category Inference Routing
nodes.description: Dialogue, simulation, intent, and reaction inference can resolve independent providers, models, and keys over a prioritized three-lane queue.

nodes.label: Rundale Documentation Hub
nodes.description: Master navigation hub organizing durable design, speculative ideas, active and archived plans, ADRs, requirements, research, development guides, and agent references.

nodes.label: Roadmap Status Authority
nodes.description: The feature-status matrix in requirements/roadmap.md is declared authoritative; the index provides an orientation summary and purpose-based status vocabulary.

nodes.label: Purpose-Based Document Taxonomy
nodes.description: Documentation is classified by purpose and lifecycle: durable design, speculative ideas, active plans, archived plans, and architectural decisions, each with explicit status vocabulary.

nodes.label: Active Visual Client Direction
nodes.description: The semantic chat-first shell with responsive DOM art is the active default; Pixi notebook, diorama, and Godot tracks are retained as retired, proposed, or exploratory records.

nodes.label: 1820s Ireland Research Archive
nodes.description: A structured research collection grounds language, society, material culture, economy, institutions, spirituality, environment, and historical context used by world-building and NPC dialogue.

nodes.label: Maybe Bad Ideas Scope-Risk Register
nodes.description: A deliberately noncommittal holding area records potentially valuable but risky ideas such as animals and generational NPC life, preventing loss without implying commitment.

nodes.label: Multi-Provider Inference Graduated From Idea
nodes.description: LM Studio and cloud model support is struck from the speculative list and marked shipped, demonstrating that the register distinguishes realized ideas from unresolved scope risks.

nodes.label: Google OAuth Configuration
nodes.description: Optional Google sign-in requires client ID, client secret, and public URL environment variables plus consent-screen scopes and exact callback registration.

nodes.label: Exact OAuth Redirect URI Contract
nodes.description: The registered Google callback must byte-for-byte match the server-computed public URL plus /auth/callback/google, including scheme and port.

nodes.label: OAuth Silent Disable Behavior
nodes.description: When either credential is absent or empty, OAuth routes are not registered and sign-in is silently disabled rather than startup failing.

nodes.label: Release Tag as Single Source of Truth
nodes.description: A vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH tag is the release authority; the release script synchronizes three user-visible version fields and the tag-triggered workflow validates their agreement.

nodes.label: Two-Level Release Dry Run
nodes.description: Local dry-run verifies version diffs without writes, while manually dispatched CI builds an artifact without publishing a release; tag pushes alone authorize publication.

nodes.label: Linux-Only Release Scope
nodes.description: The current pipeline publishes only a Linux x86_64 binary tarball and explicitly excludes desktop bundles, crates.io/npm publishing, and changelog generation.

nodes.label: Repository Workspace Orientation

nodes.label: Cross-Platform Setup Guide
nodes.description: Installation and build guidance for Rust 2024, Node 20+, Tauri, local inference, and platform-specific native dependencies on macOS, Linux, and Windows.

nodes.label: Hardware-Aware Local Model Selection
nodes.description: Users can pre-pull Gemma 4 tiers matched to available VRAM or unified memory, with smaller edge models supporting constrained or CPU-only hosts.

nodes.label: Platform-Native GUI Dependencies
nodes.description: Tauri builds depend on Xcode tools and WebKit equivalents on macOS/Linux, MSVC and WebView2 on Windows, and an X display or xvfb for headless Linux GUI capture.

nodes.label: Paired Inference and Transcript Artifacts
nodes.description: Each backend writes paired JSONL logs for raw inference calls and user-visible game events so strange behavior can be reproduced and reported.

nodes.label: Request-ID Dialogue Traceability
nodes.description: NPC dialogue transcript events carry request IDs that match inference records, allowing a visible reply to be traced directly to its generating prompt and response.

nodes.label: Inference Log Secret Redaction Boundary
nodes.description: Known API-key and authorization-token shapes are redacted before disk writes, while gameplay content remains verbatim for reproducibility and therefore requires review before sharing.

nodes.label: ADR-001 Named Location Graph Decision
nodes.description: Accepted decision to model the world as authored named location nodes with weighted traversal edges, dynamic context, and optional mythological properties.

nodes.label: Text-Adventure Spatial Abstraction
nodes.description: A graph was preferred over grids, continuous coordinates, and procedural generation because named destinations match language interaction and real Irish geography without unused spatial precision.

nodes.label: ADR-002 Four-Tier Resource Allocation
nodes.description: Accepted cognitive LOD decision assigns full dialogue, nearby light inference, distant batch inference, and far-away CPU rules according to player proximity.

nodes.label: State Inflation and Cross-Tier Coherence
nodes.description: Sparse distant state is inflated into rich context when the player approaches, while an event bus must preserve coherent changes across tier boundaries.

nodes.label: ADR-003 Three-Layer WAL Persistence
nodes.description: Accepted SQLite WAL design combines real-time append-only journal events, periodic background snapshots, and named branch references.

nodes.label: Crash Recovery Without Gameplay Stutter
nodes.description: Journal replay protects recent progress while spawn_blocking and WAL concurrency keep synchronous database work from blocking the async game loop.

nodes.label: ADR-004 Git-Like Timeline Decision
nodes.description: Accepted save model maps journal, snapshot, branch, fork, and load operations to version-control concepts for invisible persistence and alternate timelines.

nodes.label: Independent Branch Clocks
nodes.description: Each save branch retains its own in-game time and unplayed branches do not advance, preventing temporal paradoxes while supporting experimentation.

nodes.label: ADR-005 Ollama Local Inference Baseline
nodes.description: Accepted Ollama REST backend keeps inference private, offline-capable, and cost-free while allocating different model sizes to dialogue, simulation, and intent workloads.

nodes.label: Background-Lane Critic Escape Hatch
nodes.description: Ollama remains the v1 runtime, but recurring visible response-swap flicker or critic p95 above 1500 ms triggers written reassessment of vLLM/TGI rather than an ad-hoc switch.

nodes.label: ADR-006 Natural Language to Structured Intent
nodes.description: Accepted input flow checks reliable slash commands first and otherwise parses free-form player language into typed action intent JSON, asking for clarification when unresolved.
nodes.norm_label: adr-006 natural language to structured intent

nodes.label: Guess-the-Verb Rejection
nodes.description: Rigid parsers, keyword matching, and choice menus were rejected because they constrain natural expression; inference latency is accepted to preserve literary agency.

nodes.label: ADR-007 Superseded 20-Minute Day
nodes.description: The original accepted 20-real-minute game day was superseded because it felt too fast; Normal is now 40 minutes with selectable presets retaining the original as Fast.

nodes.label: Seasonal Visibility Pacing Goal
nodes.description: Compressed time is intended to make seasons, festivals, relationship evolution, and parish change visible within ordinary play while respecting inference budgets.

nodes.label: ADR-008 Typed LLM Output Schema
nodes.description: Accepted decision constrains NPC cognition and player-intent responses to JSON schemas that can deterministically update state while retaining hidden internal thought.

nodes.label: Partial-Parse Resilience
nodes.description: Serde defaults, partial extraction, and clarification fallbacks trade schema overhead and constrained creativity for reliable state processing of imperfect local-model output.

nodes.label: ADR-009 Authentic Geography, Fictional Identity
nodes.description: Accepted world-building decision uses real Irish places, roads, townlands, and landmarks while requiring fictional people, businesses, institutions, disclaimer text, and source attribution.

nodes.label: Geographic Data License Obligations
nodes.description: OSM-derived databases carry ODbL attribution/share-alike obligations and Tailte Eireann material carries CC-BY attribution obligations.

nodes.label: ADR-010 Five-Layer Prompt-Injection Defense
nodes.description: Accepted defense-in-depth design combines role separation, delimited and sandwiched input, boundary sanitization, typed output validation, and display-path filtering.

nodes.label: Typed Validation as State-Integrity Safety Net
nodes.description: Schema checks, enum validation, numeric clamps, reference checks, and neutral fallbacks are the strongest layer because they prevent malformed or injected output from mutating canonical state.
nodes.norm_label: typed validation as state-integrity safety net

nodes.label: Proportionate Local Threat Model
nodes.description: Defenses target accidental injection, immersion breaks, leakage, and state corruption in a single-player local game rather than claiming adversarial security against a determined player with source access.

nodes.label: ADR-011 Separate Geo-Tool OSM Pipeline
nodes.description: Accepted parish-geo-tool binary downloads targeted Overpass data, extracts features and roads, creates period templates, preserves curated content, and emits validated world JSON using shared engine types.

nodes.label: Description Provenance Tiers
nodes.description: Curated descriptions are immutable, template descriptions are rule-generated, and llm_pending entries are eligible for later enrichment, with sidecar provenance tracking.

nodes.label: ADR-012 Progressive Documentation Hierarchy
nodes.description: Accepted layered documentation hierarchy minimizes context cost through entry points, a navigation hub, status/planning, design, decisions/reference, and development operations.

nodes.label: Documentation Status Reconciliation Contract
nodes.description: Roadmap status is authoritative, index and plan summaries must agree with it, and phase completion historically required coordinated updates across four locations.

nodes.label: ADR-013 Optional Cloud Dialogue Routing
nodes.description: Accepted hybrid routing sends player-facing Tier 1 dialogue to an optional cloud model for quality and speed while keeping simulation and intent local; absent cloud configuration preserves local-only behavior.

nodes.label: Dialogue Quality, Cost, and Offline Tradeoff
nodes.description: Cloud dialogue improves player-facing quality and frees local resources but adds token cost and network dependence; the static local fallback maintains offline play.

nodes.label: Ambient Sound System
nodes.rationale: Period-correct sound is selected from location, time, season, and weather so the world is heard as a connected parish rather than as isolated scenes.

nodes.label: Graph-Based Sound Propagation
nodes.rationale: BFS over traversal-time edges lets bells, music, and animals carry beyond their source while weather, indoor walls, and distance attenuate volume.

nodes.label: In-App Bug Report Tool
nodes.rationale: Players and QA agents share one reproducible reporting path that bundles screenshot, logs, world state, and contextual debug records.

nodes.label: Safe Bug-Report Dry-Run Fallback
nodes.rationale: Outward GitHub writes require an explicit token; CI and sandboxes instead persist the composed report to disk.

nodes.label: Cognitive Level-of-Detail
nodes.rationale: NPC fidelity decreases with distance so hundreds of characters can maintain ongoing lives within finite inference capacity.

nodes.label: Four-Tier Cognition Policy
nodes.rationale: Immediate NPCs use rich inference, nearby and distant NPCs use progressively cheaper model work, and far-away NPCs use deterministic CPU rules.

nodes.label: Debug System
nodes.rationale: Runtime visibility covers NPC state, inference, background tasks, logs, and performance while compiling entirely out of non-debug builds.

nodes.label: Bounded Debug Telemetry
nodes.rationale: Watch channels and ring buffers provide latest-value diagnostics without unbounded queues or release-build overhead.

nodes.label: Debug Snapshot UI
nodes.rationale: A single serializable DebugSnapshot is the cross-runtime contract for five live inspection tabs.

nodes.label: Inference Call Inspector
nodes.rationale: The UI exposes latency, request shape, full prompts, responses, and errors for individual inference calls.

nodes.label: Parish Designer
nodes.rationale: A shared Svelte editor and backend module replace error-prone hand editing while preserving Tauri/web mode parity.

nodes.label: Running-Game Isolation
nodes.rationale: EditorState loads a fresh disk copy and never mutates live AppState, preventing tick races, autosave corruption, and memory/file divergence.

nodes.label: Clean Mod Round-Trip Invariant
nodes.rationale: Saving an unchanged mod must produce an empty git diff; granular loading preserves raw optional fields and avoids loader post-processing.

nodes.label: Manual IPC Type Synchronization
nodes.rationale: Manual TypeScript mirrors remain because one frontend and an existing parity sensor do not justify generator dependencies and lost frontend-facing comments.

nodes.label: Two-Direction IPC Parity Sensor
nodes.rationale: A field manifest plus Rust serialization and TypeScript source tests turn missed contract edits into CI failures.

nodes.label: Game Quality Control System
nodes.rationale: Stateful 100-turn live playtests measure game quality, persist artifacts, track regressions, and feed discrete findings into the fix backlog.

nodes.label: Gate Plus Quality Scoring
nodes.rationale: Deterministic hard failures gate a run before seven session-level judge axes can form a weighted quality score; rubric hashes make verdicts auditable.

nodes.label: Harness Finding-to-Fix Closed Loop
nodes.rationale: Canonical finding signatures deduplicate issue filing, automated backlog work fixes the defect, and later runs show recovery against git history.

nodes.label: parish-harness Crate
nodes.rationale: The opt-in tool observes a live backend over public IPC and adds no gameplay behavior.

nodes.label: Live Harness Proof Contract
nodes.rationale: Proof requires a real run summary, persisted run/turn/axis rows, nonblank frames, and architecture-fitness evidence rather than a synthetic gameplay fixture.

nodes.label: parish-geo-tool
nodes.rationale: OpenStreetMap features are classified, connected, described, merged with curation, and validated into a Parish world graph.

nodes.label: Curated and Generated Geography Provenance
nodes.rationale: Description tiers prevent regenerated template or LLM-pending content from overwriting human-authored locations.

nodes.label: Godot Presentation Client and Parish Sidecar
nodes.rationale: Godot owns presentation while the Rust Parish runtime remains the authoritative simulation and persistence engine.
nodes.norm_label: godot presentation client and parish sidecar

nodes.label: Authoritative State Boundary
nodes.rationale: Godot may interpolate visual feel locally but consequential state changes go through Parish and stale render caches yield to sequenced authoritative events.

nodes.label: Human-Approved Gameplay Geometry
nodes.rationale: AI may propose pixels, but humans own map interpretation, doors, paths, navigation masks, and final consistency.

nodes.label: Tauri and Svelte Game GUI
nodes.rationale: The player-facing shell combines a streaming story log, map, nearby characters, Irish word hints, status, and natural-language input.

nodes.label: Player-Centered Parish Map
nodes.rationale: A local minimap follows the player while a full overlay supports parish-wide pan, zoom, labels, and adjacent travel.

nodes.label: Harness Strangler Migration
nodes.rationale: The legacy harness remains the oracle while a scriptable inference mock and real event emitter expose divergence from the shipping game loop before ownership changes.

nodes.label: Harness Divergence Ledger
nodes.rationale: Normalized lockstep results record each legacy-versus-real mismatch, with minimal normalization audited to avoid masking true differences.

nodes.label: Quality-Harness Skill Run Ingest
nodes.rationale: Agent-driven quality-harness runs enter the same database and dashboard as binary-produced runs with equivalent axes, findings, frames, and cost.

nodes.label: Single Harness Persistence Seam
nodes.rationale: Ingest reuses the live run persistence functions so scored and gated semantics cannot drift into a second write path.

nodes.label: Illustrated Notebook Pixi Experiment
nodes.rationale: The Pixi canvas, renderer, and overlay contracts were removed; approved scene plates and portraits survived for the chat-first shell.

nodes.label: Persistent Notebook Interaction Model
nodes.rationale: Notebook tabs turn one sewn page in place, while maps and interruptive utilities use dismissible sheets that preserve scene, draft, tab, and focus.

nodes.label: Independent NPC Agents
nodes.rationale: Agency is persisted as individual agendas and wake times, not modeled as one operating-system task or inference context per NPC.

nodes.label: Collect-Plan-Commit Agent Flow
nodes.rationale: Immutable snapshots release locks before planning, then one reducer validates typed intents and applies canonical mutations deterministically.

nodes.label: Persisted Agent Agenda
nodes.rationale: Goals, activity, typed plan steps, wake deadlines, interruptibility, and generation survive save/load while scheduler indexes remain ephemeral.

nodes.label: Priority-Lane Inference Queue
nodes.rationale: Interactive, background, and batch channels share one strictly prioritized single-flight worker, isolating queue bursts but not preempting an in-flight request.

nodes.label: Per-Category Inference Latency Budgets
nodes.rationale: Intent and reaction are subsecond turn-critical paths, simulation is background-bounded, and dialogue prioritizes time to first token.

nodes.label: Apple-Silicon Local Inference Evidence
nodes.rationale: Measured results show Tier 2 and cached dialogue pass, intent and reaction have p95 failures, and constrained Tier 3 batches miss the stated budget by roughly twentyfold.

nodes.label: npc-arrival-greetings Flag
nodes.rationale: Muting unsolicited arrival greetings prevents crowded scenes from erupting while first conversation still introduces the addressed NPC.

nodes.label: NPC Context System
nodes.rationale: Identity, intelligence, relationships, knowledge, immediate scene state, history, and witness awareness ground each NPC inference.

nodes.label: Witness Memory and Scene Continuity
nodes.rationale: Bystanders remember nearby exchanges and per-location logs prevent repeated introductions and disconnected dialogue.

nodes.label: Parish Engine and Rundale Mod Separation
nodes.rationale: The generic Rust engine owns simulation mechanics while all Irish setting, historical context, prompts, festivals, and presentation data live in the Rundale mod.
nodes.norm_label: parish engine and rundale mod separation

nodes.label: Shared IPC Orchestration
nodes.rationale: Tauri, web, headless, and harness delegate commands, streaming, conversations, views, and configuration to one backend-agnostic composition layer.

nodes.label: Cold MCP Registration
nodes.rationale: A no-build shim completes MCP initialization immediately in fresh worktrees and hands calls to the Rust server when its binary becomes available.

nodes.label: MCP Manifest Single Source of Truth
nodes.rationale: One committed JSON manifest defines the tool wire surface for both shim and Rust server; a name-to-translator bijection test guards executable coverage.

nodes.rationale: An append-only WorldEvent journal provides recovery, periodic GameSnapshot records bound replay, and Branch objects preserve alternative timelines.

nodes.label: NPC @Mention Targeting
nodes.rationale: Autocomplete and ordered exact, first-name, brief-name, and fallback matching make addressed dialogue explicit.

nodes.rationale: Debug commands are compiled out of release builds, while system commands remain slash-prefixed until a confirmed fuzzy prefix-free design exists.

nodes.label: Data Depth and Cognitive LOD
nodes.rationale: Sketched, Elaborated, and Authored data depth is intentionally orthogonal to four runtime cognitive tiers.

nodes.label: Pre-Generated SQLite Population
nodes.rationale: Pre-generating Sketched NPCs avoids runtime stalls and preserves referential integrity, households, and cross-parish relationships.

nodes.label: Read-Only World Database plus Save Overlay

nodes.rationale: The strategy covers deterministic harness tests, script mode, agent play-tests, evaluation baselines, and browser UI proof.

nodes.label: GameTestHarness
nodes.rationale: A synchronous typed API drives production game paths without the TUI or an LLM, making regression tests deterministic.

nodes.label: Playwright Mocked Tauri Contract
nodes.rationale: Frontend end-to-end and visual regression tests exercise UI behavior against mocked IPC while preserving command parity expectations.

nodes.label: Game Time System (Implemented)
nodes.rationale: Normal speed maps forty real minutes to one game day, with traversal advancing the same canonical clock.

nodes.label: Time Speed Presets

nodes.label: Seasonal Festival Calendar

nodes.label: Seven Weather Conditions

nodes.label: Palette-Independent Weather
nodes.rationale: The UI palette remains driven by time of day so weather semantics do not become conflated with visual clock cues.

nodes.label: Real Geography Policy (Implemented)
nodes.rationale: Rundale uses real Irish place names, coordinates, and geography while keeping inhabitants and businesses fictional.

nodes.label: Location Traversal Graph
nodes.rationale: Named location nodes and traversal-time edges support natural movement, en-route time, encounters, and distance-based resolution.

nodes.label: Historical Geography Sources
nodes.rationale: OSM, Townlands.ie, Tailte Eireann, GSI Goldmine, OS200, Rumsey, OpenHistoricalMap, and British Library collections ground the map.

nodes.label: Semantic Memory and RAG Brainstorm
nodes.rationale: The proposal addresses brittle keyword-overlap memory retrieval.

nodes.label: Hybrid Memory Retrieval
nodes.rationale: Dense embeddings and BM25 are fused with reciprocal-rank fusion across episodic, semantic, and procedural memories.

nodes.label: Semantic Memory First Cut
nodes.rationale: A parish-embeddings crate, SQLite vectors, default-off hybrid recall, and nightly reflection form the proposed incremental implementation.

nodes.label: Structured Generation Brainstorm
nodes.rationale: The proposal targets failures in sentinel-separated free text and JSON output.

nodes.label: Schema-Constrained Decoding
nodes.rationale: JsonSchema serves as source of truth for grammar-based decoding and typed tool payloads.

nodes.label: Two-Segment Streaming
nodes.rationale: Natural dialogue can stream before a separately constrained structured segment is decoded and validated.

nodes.label: Dialogue Quality Loops Brainstorm
nodes.rationale: The proposal addresses semantic anachronism and weak dialogue quality.

nodes.label: Local Dialogue Rejection Sampler
nodes.rationale: A deterministic wordlist and dialogue oracles score background candidates, with a bounded deadline and an immediate draft fallback.

nodes.label: Critic and Self-Refinement Loop
nodes.rationale: A critic, constitutional rules, retrieval style examples, uncertainty handling, and optional regeneration create a layered quality loop.

nodes.label: Agent Planning and Tools Brainstorm
nodes.rationale: The proposal adds bounded deliberation and access to authoritative world information.

nodes.label: Read-Only WorldView Tools
nodes.rationale: Locate, relationship, memory, belief, time, weather, and news queries are proposed before any world-mutating tool.

nodes.label: Bounded ReAct Loop
nodes.rationale: A maximum of three steps and a 400 ms budget limit latency and runaway behavior; mutations remain validated proposals with audit trails.

nodes.label: Inference Performance Brainstorm
nodes.rationale: The proposal addresses Ollama critical-path latency and starvation of background work.

nodes.label: Utility Inference Lane
nodes.rationale: A small model handles non-prose tasks so structured extraction, judging, and routing do not compete with dialogue generation.

nodes.label: Cache, Batch, and Speculate
nodes.rationale: KV and prompt caches, speculative decoding, batching, quantization tiers, deadlines, and preemption form the optimization portfolio.

nodes.label: Personalization and Learning Brainstorm
nodes.rationale: The proposal adapts play style while retaining a local-first privacy posture.

nodes.label: Persisted Player Profile
nodes.rationale: A parish-preferences PlayerProfile is updated nightly, stored with saves, injected into prompts, and informed by explicit feedback.

nodes.label: Opt-In Local Learning
nodes.rationale: DPO, KTO, distillation, steering, and fine-tuning are deferred until structured schemas stabilize and any upload remains opt-in.

nodes.label: Social Simulation Brainstorm
nodes.rationale: The proposal models beliefs, rumors, factions, reputation, and group scenes as explicit social state.

nodes.label: Belief and Rumor Store
nodes.rationale: Nested beliefs and content-mutating rumors make knowledge perspective-dependent rather than globally shared.

nodes.label: Joint Multi-Agent Scenes
nodes.rationale: Joint prompts and a shared blackboard coordinate multiple NPCs, with caps and a latency fallback controlling complexity.

nodes.label: Multimodal Brainstorm
nodes.rationale: The proposal extends Rundale into voice, generated art, ambient sound, visual authoring, and gesture metadata.

nodes.label: Offline Voice Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Piper streaming TTS, Whisper ASR, voice activity detection, and authoritative pronunciation overrides support local voice interaction.

nodes.label: Deterministic Visual Assets
nodes.rationale: Portrait and scene generation are treated as cached, reproducible authoring outputs rather than untracked runtime decoration.

nodes.label: AI Evaluation and Safety Brainstorm
nodes.rationale: The proposal fills quality gaps not covered by unit tests and deterministic feature proofs.

nodes.label: Golden Transcript Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Seeded transcripts, judge rubrics, latency and cost metrics, and provenance audits create repeatable AI quality evidence.

nodes.label: Adversarial Safety Suite
nodes.rationale: Prompt-injection tests, knowledge-leak and over-abstention calibration, self-play, and human review guard against unsafe or ungrounded output.

nodes.label: Knowledge Graph Grounding Brainstorm
nodes.rationale: The graph is proposed as authoritative symbolic grounding that complements fuzzy semantic memory.

nodes.label: Provenanced Fact and Belief Graph
nodes.rationale: Triples retain source, confidence, and time while authored ground truth remains separate from what each NPC believes.

nodes.label: Pre-Turn Knowledge Gate
nodes.rationale: A canonical predicate registry and pre-turn belief stanza prevent retrieved flavor text from granting unauthorized knowledge.

nodes.label: AI Director Brainstorm
nodes.rationale: The proposal introduces authored dramatic pressure without turning NPCs into puppets.

nodes.label: Authored Directed Events
nodes.rationale: A daily or adaptive director may choose at most a small number of structured pressure, entrance, crisis, celebration, or reveal archetypes from director.toml.

nodes.label: Nudges, Not Puppetry
nodes.rationale: Director output modifies opportunity and pressure while canonical NPC agency decides the response.

nodes.label: LLM-Assisted Authoring Brainstorm
nodes.rationale: The proposal accelerates mod creation while preserving authorship and historical accountability.

nodes.label: Anchored Candidate Generation
nodes.rationale: Authors supply geography and population anchors; the model proposes schedules, households, and relationships as reviewable candidates.

nodes.label: Human Review and Provenance Gate
nodes.rationale: No generated change is committed without diff review, deterministic seed and model revision, field provenance, and anachronism checks.

nodes.label: SOTA AI Techniques Brainstorm Notes
nodes.rationale: These notes are explicitly non-authoritative and must graduate into an ADR and feature flag before shipping.

nodes.label: Current AI Baseline
nodes.rationale: The baseline combines cognitive LOD, an Ollama priority queue, keyword memory, JSON separators, anachronism checks, and hand-authored content.

nodes.label: AI Technique Priority Order
nodes.rationale: Semantic memory, structured generation, and the utility inference lane come first; tools, knowledge graph, and director follow; learning and authoring arrive last.

nodes.label: ADR and Feature-Flag Graduation Gate
nodes.rationale: A brainstorm item is not a committed plan until its decision, risks, rollout, and runtime control become an accepted ADR and feature flag.

nodes.label: Graphics V2 Research Governance
nodes.rationale: The folder authority classifies graphics artifacts as exploratory design references rather than production runtime assets, requires preservation and sidecar provenance, and records which cycles are recipe evidence, edited visual targets, or negative results.

nodes.label: Clean-Context Recipe Evidence Discipline
nodes.rationale: Reproducible claims require isolated map-reader, control, prompt, render, and audit stages with declared inputs and saved outputs; coordinator image generation or contexts exposed to prior failures are explicitly weaker evidence.

nodes.label: Historic Map Veto Authority
nodes.rationale: Historic map crops remain the source of truth for feature existence, orientation, and topology; generated controls and style references are subordinate and must not materialize uncertain survey lines, scenic layouts, or leaked landmarks.

nodes.label: Graphics V2 Research Index
nodes.rationale: The exploratory index routes work among current chat surfaces, retired notebook proposals, background-plate experiments, map interpretation, runtime layers, interiors, portraits, and alternate clients while keeping generated research separate from shipped authority.

nodes.label: Beechwood BJ Notebook Visual Target
nodes.rationale: BJ is the strongest bounded Beechwood Q/M repaint because it preserves compound topology while improving notebook texture, doors, and roof discipline, but it is explicitly visual-target evidence rather than one-shot recipe proof.

nodes.label: Cycle BL Soft-Garden Next Run
nodes.rationale: The preferred next clean-context run is BL, superseding BK, to soften BJ's remaining regular survey-like garden rows without changing north-up topology, adding walling, weakening doors, or importing unsupported semantics.

nodes.label: Roscommon Hedgerow-Bank-Ditch Boundary Prior
nodes.rationale: Source-backed regional guidance makes hedgerows, banks, ditches, remnant hedges, and stone-earthen banks the default for ordinary County Roscommon boundaries, reserving continuous stone walls for corroborated rocky, yard, gate, road, or local-landscape contexts.

nodes.label: Authentic Irish Dry-Stone Wall Visual Contract
nodes.rationale: Source-supported walls must be mortarless and irregular, using locally gathered mixed stones, gaps, chinks, uneven coping, vegetation, and broken silhouettes; uniform blocks, ashlar, brick courses, cobble chains, and gray bead walls fail.
nodes.norm_label: authentic irish dry-stone wall visual contract

nodes.label: Five-Stage Kilteevan Exterior Pipeline Run
nodes.rationale: A per-location checklist requires saved source, reader, control, camera, prompt, render, audit, and comparison artifacts across separate map-reader, control-builder, prompt-builder, render, and independent-audit roles, ending in an explicit evidence disposition.

nodes.label: Plate-First Historic Map Crop Selection
nodes.rationale: The desired 16:9 playable plate, orthographic camera, north-up orientation, sprite scale, local site, and exits are fixed first; the historic crop is then derived as geography evidence rather than allowed to dictate a high survey composition.

nodes.label: Reproducible Clean-Context Map Reader Stage
nodes.rationale: A uniform rubric turns a single historic crop into confidence-graded observations about corridors, buildings, planting, physical and administrative boundaries, negative evidence, and uncertainties without using lore, style targets, or prior renders.

nodes.label: Confidence-Graded Soft Disambiguation Notes
nodes.rationale: Saved reader notes may influence high-confidence geometry strongly but remain subordinate to the crop; medium and low confidence must stay generic, ambiguous, omitted, or explicitly nonphysical rather than becoming hard render instructions.

nodes.label: Map-to-Background-Plate Research Pipeline
nodes.rationale: The broader research path replaces freeform topology invention with a saved chain from source crop through reproducible map reading, optional controls, clean prompt/render stages, and independent audit; it now defers active Kilteevan work to the stricter BU-style pipeline.

nodes.label: Subagent-Gated BU-Style Exterior Pipeline
nodes.rationale: The current reusable Kilteevan exterior procedure fixes map authority, clean-context role separation, required artifact bundles, geometry-before-style ordering, one fresh render, independent auditing, and at most one bounded correction; it is explicitly not yet a production batch renderer.

nodes.label: Grove BZ Pass with Boundary Caveat
nodes.rationale: BZ proves the complete staged workflow can preserve one Grove topology, camera, doors, and BU-style realism, but ambiguous edges still became excessive blocky stone walls, blocking production batch readiness until multiple distinct topologies pass the same boundary-material gate.
nodes.norm_label: grove bz pass with boundary caveat

nodes.label: Cleanroom One-Shot Background Plate Test
nodes.rationale: One-shot prompt evaluation must use a fresh context and only declared generic inputs, then judge camera, north-up topology, playable connectivity, boundary interpretation, doors, absence constraints, and smoke-free layering; batch trust requires two independent passing generations.

nodes.label: Portable Background Plate Prompt Contract
nodes.rationale: A self-contained reusable prompt orders walkable orthographic projection, map-derived navigation, topology, notebook style, historical architecture, and beauty while enforcing north-up scale, local hub cropping, raw-map vetoes, regional boundary priors, authentic walls, fitted doors, and dynamic-layer exclusions.

nodes.label: Canonical Neutral Location Plate
nodes.rationale: One neutral low-oblique plate should own stable visual geometry, projection, roads, doors, yards, gates, and paths; full alternate plates are reserved for large physical changes because generated variants drift in topology and sprite scale.

nodes.label: Runtime Masks, Sockets, Overlays, and Actor Stack
nodes.rationale: Time, weather, season, occupancy, props, characters, creatures, lights, smoke, and events belong in aligned masks, typed sockets, decals, particles, sprites, and color grades over the canonical plate, with a defined render order and minimum production bundle.
nodes.norm_label: runtime masks, sockets, overlays, and actor stack

nodes.rationale: Generate one continuous supertile first and split it mechanically; this preserved seams and exact reassembly.

nodes.rationale: Styling tiles independently produced a materially worse seam ratio than the source and mosaic-first paths.

nodes.label: Safe-Center Overlap Join Failure

nodes.label: Masked Semantic Seam Repair
nodes.rationale: Broad seam repair can reduce a visible seam but remains useful only with masks, semantic overlays, and source audit.

nodes.label: Exact Mechanical Reassembly
nodes.rationale: Mosaic-first and continuous-panel splits achieved zero reassembly error.
